abstract: Mr. President and gentlemen, I feel it an honour to be called upon, as a mere stranger, to read a paper before members of this Institute. I have only been in the country about three months, and already I have been given an opportunity of addressing you — as I say, I consider it an honour. As this paper has been written, or rather these tests taken and graphs drawn, at very short notice, I hope you will excuse its obvious deficiencies. I can hardly call it a paper, as I only propose to show some graphs drawn from test figures taken during the last three weeks, and point out their chief characteristics.

abstract: It is always a matter of some small difficulty to discuss a descriptive paper, and the difficulty is increased rather than diminished when the paper ascends to the height of nearly absolute completeness, as in the present case. It is not often that we are so fortunate as to secure such an abundance of detail as the author has collected, obviously at the expenditure of much painstaking labour. If, on the one hand. the would-be discusser experiences a difficulty in finding suitable points of departure for criticism either constructive or destructive, on the other hand he will find many reasons for expressing appreciation of the author's work, and of the work of the Railway Administration and that of their advisers. In view of certain developments within the last 18 months, it is well to remember that the decision to electrify was based on the recommendation of most highly qualified consultants, and that electrification offered the only solution to effectively cope with the traffic conditions obtaining and forecast at the time that the question was investigated.

articleTitle: Suggestions for a south african electrical development association
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Electricity supply in South Africa to-day may justly be said to have passed the problem stage. We have, generally speaking, won through those stages of development so full of interest to the engineer, the laying down of new undertakings, the enlargement or complete remodelling of existing ones, in which engineering bulks so largely. Although this kind of work will continue to demand our attention to keep paco with the development of the country, I feel the time has come when, we should go one step further than the mere provision and consider the utilisation, to the utmost, of the supply provided. I need scarcely remind the engineers in my audience that our livelihoods are all bound up in electrical development. The object of this paper is to make concrete suggestions as to how wc can actively and practically forward such development, and the solution I have to offer is the formation of a South African Electrical Development Association.

articleTitle: The characteristics of the repulsion-induction type of motor
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The study of single-phase induction motors is of importance to the electrical engineer because of their application to the problem of alternating current traction. The application of alternating current power to traction has so many obvious advantages, both practical and economical, that its use for that purpose seems natural and desirable. The difficulty has been to obtain a satisfactory single-phase motor that would fulfil all the requirements of a traction motor. Polyphase motors are not suitable for traction owing to the complexity introduced into overhead track equipment. Consequently we may say that the whole question of alternating current traction is bound up with the development of the single-phase motor. For the vast majority of industrial requirements the single-phase motor can never be a serious competitor to the polyphase machine with its simplicity, efficiency and excellent operating characteristics.

articleTitle: Photometry and the testing of incandescent lamps
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Photometry and illumination having occupied a considerable portion of this Institute's proceedings recently, the authors of this contribution feel that the results of some experiments in photometry conducted at the University of the Witwatersrand might be of interest to the members. The experiments were conducted to determine the percentage absorption of light emitted by the filaments of incandescent lamps by the standard types of bulbs enclosing them. It is an established fact that for good illumination glare is not desirable, and the light emitted from any given source should be dispersed as much as possible. This dispersion effect cannot be obtained without absorption, since it is necessary for the lamp bulb to be capable of causing internal light reflection and so scatter the light in all directions. Lack of these reflections means a loss of light and when it finally emerges it is considerably reduced. The ideal aimed at in all types of bulbs is maximum dispersion with minimum absorption. Absorption causes a considerable reduction in the efficiency of a lamp which is already a very inefficient device and may cause a considerable, increase in the power required for the same illumination as compared with the ordinary clear glass covers. It should be borne in mind that a dispersion bulb with a high percentage absorption is not necessarily inferior to a lamp with a small absorption, if in the second case the dispersion is not as good as the first.

articleTitle: Street traffic control by electrically-operated equipment
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Public streets are considered one of the most valuable utilities possessed by a community under present-day conditions, and in business operations their use is all important. Heavy investment of public funds is necessary for the construction and maintenance of streets, and to obtain a maximum return on this investment they must be utilised with a maximum of efficiency. An important factor is the time required for traffic movement; the more expeditiously both vehicular and pedestrian traffic is moved, the greater the return on the investment. Public convenience, how-ever, demands consideration, and the speed of movement should be the maximum con-sistent with safety and efficiency.

articleTitle: Presidential address by lieut.-colonel J. stewart ross, V.D.
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Mr. Pickles, in referring to my election as your President for this year, remarked on my diffidence in accepting the honour, an honour which I highly appreciate. I now confess that the preparation of a Presidential address worthy of submission to a learned body of members such as this Institute possesses was one of the main causes of my diffidence. Having for more than two-thirds of my life moved in an atmosphere and environment where the belief prevailed that the “sword was mightier than the pen,” and where it was thought that alertness and prompt action yielded better results than profound judgment or exact knowledge, the wielding of the pen became to me a lost art. Therefore, gentlemen, I must crave your indulgence if my address falls far short of the high standard set by my predecessors in the Presidential chair. While the foregoing reasons may account for the doubtful literary quality of my address, they do not justify its parochial nature. That is due to design. I justify the local and parochial aspect of my address because I believe the subject affects our endeavours in this country more than in older countries with established industries, customs, precedents, and because of that modern method which has no thought for posterity and the effect it is going to have upon the future intelligence of the human race, that is, the one-man-one-job method.

abstract: In compiling a paper on the subject of “Modern Illumination,” my chief difficulty has been to deal adequately with what is a very large subject. Each section of this subject could constitute a paper in itself.
